subject: English
description: Active to passive: simple tenses, modals, imperatives, questions

questions.stem: Convert to passive: 'The chef cooks delicious meals.'

options.option_text: Delicious meals were cooked by the chef.
Delicious meals are cooked by the chef.
Delicious meals are being cooked by chef.
The chef is cooked by delicious meals.

questions.explanation: Active 'cooks' (simple present) → passive: is/are + V3. Subject + verb + object → object + auxiliary + V3 + by + subject. 'meals are cooked by the chef'. Distractor 1 = past tense (was/were). Distractor 3 = present continuous. Distractor 4 = subject-object swap with wrong logic.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Convert: 'The teacher is teaching the students.' (present continuous → passive)

options.option_text: Students are taught by the teacher.
Students are being taught by the teacher.
Students were taught by the teacher.
Students have been taught by the teacher.

questions.explanation: Continuous → passive: is/are + being + V3. 'is teaching' → 'is being taught'. Distractor 1 = simple present. Distractor 3 = simple past. Distractor 4 = present perfect.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Convert: 'They have built a new bridge.' (present perfect → passive)

options.option_text: A new bridge is built by them.
A new bridge has been built by them.
A new bridge was being built by them.
A new bridge will be built by them.

questions.explanation: Present perfect → passive: has/have been + V3. 'have built' → 'has been built' (matching 'a bridge'). Distractor 1 = simple present. Distractor 3 = past continuous. Distractor 4 = future.

questions.stem: Convert (modal): 'You must complete this work.' to passive:

options.option_text: This work must complete by you.
This work must be completed by you.
This work is must completed by you.
You must be completed this work.

questions.explanation: Modal verbs (must, can, should, will, may, might, could) → passive: modal + be + V3. 'must complete' → 'must be completed'. Same for other modals: 'can do' → 'can be done'; 'should write' → 'should be written'.
questions.subject: English

options.option_text: The window must be opened by you.
Let the window be opened.
Window opens itself in there.
You should open the window now.

questions.explanation: IMPERATIVE → passive: 'Let + object + be + V3'. 'Open the window' → 'Let the window BE OPENED'. For NEGATIVE imperatives: 'Don't open' → 'Let the window not be opened'. For requests: 'Please help me' → 'You are requested to help me' / 'Let me be helped'. Distractor 1 — adds modal 'must'. Distractor 3 — meaning lost. Distractor 4 — different sense.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Convert (question): 'Who wrote this letter?' to passive:

options.option_text: By whom was this letter written?
Whom is the letter written by?
Who is wrote this letter?
By whom is this letter being written?

questions.explanation: Wh-questions in passive: keep wh-word; restructure with auxiliary. 'Who wrote' → 'By whom + was + written?' (subject becomes object of preposition 'by'). Tense: simple past (wrote → was written). Distractor 2 — informal but past tense missing. Distractor 3 — wrong grammar. Distractor 4 — wrong tense (continuous).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Convert: 'They will solve the problem.' to passive:

options.option_text: The problem is solved by them.
The problem will be solved by them.
The problem will being solved by them.
The problem has solved by them.

questions.explanation: Simple future → passive: will be + V3. 'will solve' → 'will be solved'. Distractor 1 = simple present. Distractor 3 = wrong grammar. Distractor 4 = present perfect missing 'been'.
